topic_ko: 양자 인간 — 영구히 정착하기 어려워진 세계
_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 31번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다.

passage: The map of where humanity actually lives is losing its once-firm outlines.
Because relocation has become an ordinary part of life, our species is undergoing something like a change of state.
Matter melts from solid to liquid and then evaporates into gas as its molecules warm, drift apart and quicken.
Human beings now behave in much the same way, resembling quantum particles whose speed and position never hold still.
Many people would welcome a return to some older form of steadiness.
Yet a quantum world simply does not offer that comfort to anyone who asks for it.
The sheer complexity of modern life keeps making it harder to stay in one place for good.
Wealthy remote workers, billionaires holding several passports and migrant laborers alike all belong to this expanding population.
choices: how scientific metaphors have replaced older ways of studying society
why migrant laborers earn far less than wealthy remote workers do
how growing mobility makes permanent settlement increasingly hard
why quantum physics has become the leading science of our century
how national borders are being redrawn by international agreements
theme.explanation_ko: 사람들이 늘 이동하면서 인간 지리가 상변화를 겪고, 그 결과 어디에도 영구히 정착하기 어려워졌다는 내용. '증가하는 이동성이 영구 정착을 어렵게 한다'가 주제이다. ③이 정답.
theme.distractor_ko: ①과학적 비유의 대체, ②계층 간 소득 격차, ④양자 물리학의 위상, ⑤국경 재획정은 본문의 초점이 아니다.

passage: We should stop assuming that a single permanent address is the normal shape of a human life.
People today find themselves on the move as a matter of routine rather than as an exception.
Our collective condition resembles matter warming from solid into liquid and finally into gas.
Like quantum particles, we now have speeds and positions that refuse to settle into fixed values.
Longing for the old stability is understandable, but that longing will not change how the world works.
The complexity of modern life keeps making lifelong residence in one spot harder to secure.
Digital nomads, multi-passport billionaires and migrant workers all live inside this same reality.
Our policies and expectations therefore need to be built around mobility rather than around permanence.
choices: 국가는 이주 노동자의 국경 이동을 더 엄격히 제한해야 한다.
사회의 제도와 통념은 영구 정착이 아니라 이동성을 전제로 다시 세워야 한다.
양자 물리학은 사회 현상을 설명하는 도구로 쓰이지 말아야 한다.
고소득 원격 근무자는 자신이 머무는 지역에 더 오래 정착해야 한다.
사람들은 과거의 안정된 생활 방식으로 서둘러 돌아가야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 이동이 예외가 아니라 일상이 된 세계에서 안정으로의 회귀를 바라기보다 이동성을 전제로 제도와 기대를 다시 세워야 한다는 주장. ②가 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①이주 제한, ③학문적 비유 금지, ④정착 권고, ⑤과거 회귀는 본문 주장과 어긋나거나 무관하다.

passage: Where human beings belong on the map is becoming genuinely hard to state.
Constant movement has turned into an ordinary condition rather than a rare event.
The shift resembles matter heating up so that its molecules loosen, separate and vibrate faster.
People now act like quantum particles whose velocity and location are never fixed.
A return to the old steadiness would be pleasant, yet the quantum world does not permit it.
Modern complexity instead makes permanent residence anywhere ever more difficult.
The group living this way spans both the very rich and the poorly paid.
Nomadic professionals and migrant workers together form one growing global population.
choices: 물질의 상변화는 인간 사회를 설명하기에 지나치게 단순한 비유이다.
부유층과 이주 노동자의 이동 동기는 서로 완전히 다르다.
사람들이 늘 이동하게 되면서 어디에도 영구히 정착하기 어려워지고 있다.
안정된 거주지를 확보하는 일이 여전히 삶의 가장 중요한 목표이다.
양자 물리학의 발전이 현대인의 생활 방식을 직접 바꾸어 놓았다.
gist.explanation_ko: 이동이 일상이 되면서 인간의 위치가 늘 유동적이 되었고, 그 결과 영구 정착이 어려워졌다는 것이 요지. ③이 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①비유의 한계, ②계층별 동기 차이, ④정착의 중요성, ⑤물리학의 직접적 영향은 요지가 아니다.

passage: Human geography, the record of where we actually live, is blurring at its edges.
Regular movement has heated our collective life the way warmth loosens the molecules of a solid.
Solids melt, liquids evaporate, and the particles drift further apart while vibrating faster.
Humanity now looks much the same: speeds and positions that will not stay put.
It would be pleasant to slide back toward some earlier stability.
A quantum world, however, does not run on that kind of logic.
Instead, modern complexity makes staying anywhere forever steadily harder.
From passport-collecting billionaires to migrant laborers, a varied global population now lives this way.
choices: Why Quantum Physics Explains Everything About Society
The Vanishing Address: Life in a World That Will Not Settle
How Migrant Workers Built the Modern Global Economy
Returning Home: The Comforting Power of Stability
Solid, Liquid, Gas: A Short History of Matter
title.explanation_ko: 고정된 주소, 즉 영구 정착이 사라지는 세계를 압축한 ②가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①물리학 만능론, ③이주 노동자의 경제 기여, ④안정으로의 회귀, ⑤물질의 역사는 글의 초점이 아니다.

passage: It is getting genuinely hard to say where any given person belongs on the map.
Movement has become routine, and our shared condition has warmed the way a solid warms.
Molecules loosen from one another, spread out and vibrate faster as heat rises.
People now behave similarly, with speeds and positions that never come to rest.
Many would like to slide back toward stability, but the world no longer runs that way.
The old anchor has been pulled up, and the rope hangs loose in the current.
Modern complexity keeps making permanent residence anywhere harder to secure.
Wealthy nomads and migrant laborers alike belong to this growing global population.
implication.underlined: The old anchor has been pulled up, and the rope hangs loose in the current
choices: people have lost the fixed attachments that once held them in one place
sailors and travelers now face far more dangerous ocean conditions
modern societies have deliberately abandoned all of their traditions
governments no longer keep accurate records of where citizens live
physical objects behave unpredictably when they are heated rapidly
implication.explanation_ko: '닻이 올려지고 밧줄이 물살에 느슨히 흔들린다'는 비유는 사람들을 한곳에 붙들어 두던 고정된 결속이 사라졌다는 뜻이다. ①이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ②항해의 위험, ③전통의 의도적 폐기, ④행정 기록의 부실, ⑤물체의 물리적 반응은 비유의 의미와 다르다.

passage: Human geography is becoming unclear as movement turns into an everyday condition.
We are experiencing a phase shift like the one that occurs when matter turns from solid to gas.
Molecules heat up and loosen from one another, vibrating more rapidly than before.
One might even say that humans are becoming like particles in quantum physics.
It would be nice returning to some form of stability, but a quantum world does not work that way.
The complexity of today's world makes it increasingly difficult to settle permanently anywhere.
Wealthy nomads as well as migrant workers are part of this growing global demographic.
grammar.explanation_ko: ③ 가주어 It이 앞에 나왔으므로 진주어는 to부정사여야 한다. returning이 아니라 to return으로 고쳐야 한다. ③이 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①선행사 the one을 받는 주격 관계대명사 that, ②능동 분사구문 vibrating, ③가목적어 it, ⑤A as well as B에서 앞 주어에 맞춘 are는 모두 옳다.

passage: Human geography is becoming unclear as constant movement turns into an ordinary condition.
We are experiencing a phase shift like the change of matter from solid to liquid to gas.
As heat rises, molecules tighten from one another and vibrate more rapidly.
Humans are becoming like particles in quantum physics, their velocity and location always in flux.
It would be nice to return to some form of stability, but a quantum world does not allow it.
The complexity of today's world makes it increasingly difficult to settle permanently anywhere.
Migratory workers and wealthy nomads alike belong to this diverse global demographic.
vocab.explanation_ko: ② 열이 오르면 분자 결합은 '느슨해지므로(loosen)' 서로 '조여진다(tighten)'는 정반대이다. loosen으로 고쳐야 한다. ②가 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①unclear(불분명한), ③flux(끊임없는 변화), ④settle(정착하다), ⑤diverse(다양한)는 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: The record of where human beings actually live is losing its clear outlines.
Movement has become routine, and our shared condition resembles matter warming from solid to gas.
As molecules heat, they loosen from one another, drift apart and vibrate faster.
People now behave like quantum particles whose velocity and location never come to rest.
A return to some earlier form of stability would be welcome, but the quantum world refuses it.
Instead, the complexity of modern life makes it increasingly difficult to settle permanently anywhere.
Highly paid nomads, billionaires with several passports and migrant laborers share this condition.
Together they form a varied and expanding global population of restless people.
blank.explanation_ko: 고체에서 기체로 향하는 상변화 비유와 '안정으로 돌아갈 수 없다'는 진술이 근거이다. 어려워진 것은 한곳에 영구히 머무는 일, 즉 정착이다. ③이 정답.
blank.distractor_ko: ①국경 이동과 ⑤원격 취업은 오히려 쉬워진 일이고, ②외국어 학습과 ④가족 연락은 본문에 근거가 없다.

irrelevant.intro: As regular movement becomes ordinary, human geography is losing the clear outlines it once had.
sentences: We are experiencing a phase shift much like the one matter undergoes when it warms from solid to liquid to gas.
Molecules heat up, loosen from one another and vibrate ever more rapidly as the temperature rises.
Humans now resemble quantum particles whose velocity and location remain permanently in flux.
Advances in materials science have allowed engineers to design alloys that resist heat far better than before.

irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '이동성 증가로 영구 정착이 어려워졌다'는 흐름인데 ④ '내열 합금 설계 기술의 발전'은 물질의 비유를 문자 그대로 받아 다른 주제로 빠진 무관한 문장이다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②③⑤는 모두 상변화 비유를 통해 인간의 유동성과 정착의 어려움으로 이어진다.

order.given: Human geography is becoming unclear, because people now find themselves regularly on the move.

blocks.A: One might even say that humans are becoming like particles in quantum physics, their velocity and location always in flux.
blocks.B: We are therefore experiencing a phase shift like the one matter undergoes when it turns from solid to liquid to gas, its molecules heating up and loosening from one another.
blocks.C: Returning to stability would be nice, yet a quantum world does not work that way, and modern complexity keeps making permanent settlement harder for nomads and migrant workers alike.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 '이동이 일상이 됨'을 (B)가 상변화 비유로 설명하고, (A)가 그 비유를 양자 입자로 심화하며, (C)가 안정 회귀 불가와 정착의 어려움으로 마무리한다. (B)-(A)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 '심지어 ~라고 말할 수도 있다'는 앞선 비유를 전제로 하므로 첫 순서가 될 수 없고, (C)는 결론이라 마지막이어야 한다.

insert.insert_sentence: It would be nice to return to some form of stability, but that's not how things work in a quantum world.

passage_marked.text: As people find themselves regularly on the move, we are experiencing a phase shift like the change of matter from solid to liquid to gas.
Molecules heat up and loosen from one another, vibrating more rapidly.
One might even say that humans are becoming like particles in quantum physics, their velocity and location always in flux.
Instead, the complexity of today's world makes it increasingly difficult to settle permanently anywhere.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 'a quantum world'는 바로 앞에서 양자 입자 비유가 제시된 뒤라야 자연스럽고, 뒤 문장의 'Instead'는 이 문장의 '안정 회귀 불가'를 받아야 성립한다. ④가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: 주어진 문장이 없으면 마지막 문장의 Instead가 무엇을 대신하는지 알 수 없어 논리가 끊긴다.

passage: The question of where people actually belong on the map is losing its clear answer.
Constant relocation has become an ordinary feature of contemporary life.
Our condition resembles matter warming from solid into liquid and finally into gas.
Molecules loosen from one another and vibrate faster as the heat rises.
Humans likewise now have velocities and locations that never come to rest.
A return to older forms of steadiness would be welcome but is no longer available.
Modern complexity keeps making lifelong residence in any single place harder.
Rich nomads and migrant laborers alike belong to this expanding global population.
summary.summary_template: Because movement has become __(A)__ for people across every income level, staying permanently in one place has grown steadily more __(B)__.
summary.explanation_ko: 이동이 모든 소득 계층에게 (A)routine(일상적)이 되면서, 한곳에 영구히 머무는 일은 점점 더 (B)difficult(어려운)해졌다. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 rare나 costly가 아니라 routine이고, (B)는 attractive·common·necessary가 아니라 difficult여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 Human geography + 진행형 is becoming + 보어 unclear.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 어떤 형태의 안정으로 되돌아가면 좋을 것이다.
writing.answer: It would be nice to return to some form of stability.
writing.explanation_ko: 가주어 It + would be nice + 진주어 to return ~.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 오늘날 세계의 복잡성은 어디든 영구히 정착하는 것을 점점 더 어렵게 만든다.
writing.answer: The complexity of today's world makes it increasingly difficult to settle permanently anywhere.
writing.explanation_ko: make + 가목적어 it + 형용사 difficult + 진목적어 to settle 구문.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: Humans are becoming like particles in quantum physics, their velocity and location always in ___________.
writing.explanation_ko: 속도와 위치가 '끊임없이 변하는' 상태를 뜻하는 단어는 flux이다.

writing.question: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말을 쓰시오.
writing.summary: As movement becomes (A)___________ for people at every income level, it grows harder for anyone to (B)___________ permanently in one place.
writing.explanation_ko: 이동이 일상(routine)이 되면서 한곳에 영구히 정착(settle)하기 어려워졌다는 것이 요지이다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: As people find themselves regularly on the move, we are experiencing a phase shift like when matter transitions from solid to liquid to gas.
writing.answer: 사람들이 정기적으로 이동하는 상태에 놓이면서, 우리는 물질이 고체에서 액체로, 다시 기체로 전이될 때와 같은 상변화를 겪고 있다.
writing.explanation_ko: find oneself ~(어느새 ~한 상태에 있다), phase shift(상변화), transition(전이하다).
